title: Add Actions/Responses Window Feature
description: Implement a new Actions/Responses tool window in KLogg, with UI components, filtering, COM port integration, import from JSON, and proper menu/toolbar access, as outlined in the requirements.

steps.name: Create Actions/Responses Window UI
steps.details: Define a new window (similar to the Scratchpad window) to host two tables: **Actions** and **Responses**. In the main window class, add a member for this Actions/Responses window and a QAction to toggle it, just like the existing Scratchpad:contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}:contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}. The new window contains two table views (e.g., stacked vertically with a splitter), each preceded by a live-filter QLineEdit. For the **Actions** table: Column 1 is a 'Send' button (disabled when no COM port), Column 2 is the Action name, Column 3 is a preview of the sequence. For the **Responses** table: Column 1 is an enable/disable checkbox, Column 2 is the Response name, Column 3 is a preview of the match pattern. Set each table row's tooltip to show the full description and relevant parameters (e.g., repeat/delay for actions, or comment/flags for responses).

steps.name: Implement Filter Logic for Responses
steps.details: Enable live filtering on the Responses table using KLogg's filtering engine for matching patterns. The filter text can be interpreted as plain text, hex string, or regex (same formats supported by KLogg filters). Use a QSortFilterProxyModel or similar to filter the response list based on the input: for example, if the filter looks like a hex sequence or regex, apply corresponding matching to each response's pattern. This ensures that typing a filter will narrow down the Responses entries by matching their 'match' field using the same rules as log filtering.

steps.name: COM Port Integration for Send Buttons
steps.details: Integrate the Actions table with the COM port system. All 'Send' buttons should invoke sending the respective action's sequence to the active COM port. If no COM port is open, these send buttons are greyed out (disabled). Achieve this by checking the port status and updating button enabled state whenever the port connects/disconnects. For example, connect to signals or use a status flag so that whenever there is no active connection, the UI disables the send buttons. When a COM port is active, pressing a Send button transmits the action's sequence (convert hex strings to bytes if needed) out to the port.

steps.name: Import Actions/Responses from JSON
steps.details: Provide an "Import Actions" dialog to load actions and responses from a JSON file (format matching the provided `actions.json`). Add a menu item (next to the existing 'Import Preview' if present) that opens a QFileDialog for the user to select a JSON file. Upon selection, parse the file to retrieve arrays of actions and responses. Create internal data objects or populate the table models with these entries. The JSON format includes an array of `actions` (each with fields like id, enabled, name, description, sequence type/value, and optional parameters):contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}, and an array of `responses` (each with id, enabled, name, description, a match pattern, and a response object defining action to send or special behaviors):contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}. Store the imported actions/responses in memory (similar to how preview data is stored) so that they persist during the session. If needed, save them in the application settings or session file so they can be restored like preview content.

steps.name: Add Menu and Toolbar Entries
steps.details: Make the Actions/Responses window accessible through the UI. Add a toggle action in the View menu (or Tools menu) labeled e.g. "Actions/Responses" that shows or focuses the window, similar to how the Scratchpad toggle is implemented:contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}:contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}. Also create a toolbar button with an appropriate icon that triggers the same action. The QAction should be checkable if the window can be shown/hidden, and should call a slot to show the window. Use the same pattern as showScratchPadAction: create the QAction, set icon and text, add it to the menu and toolbar, and connect it to a slot that brings up the Actions/Responses window:contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}:contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}.

steps.name: Define Data Model for Actions and Responses
steps.details: Implement data structures or models to represent Actions and Responses. For example, define classes or structs for Action and Response entries with fields as in the JSON (including sequence type/value, parameters, etc. for actions, and match type/value plus response settings for responses). Use a QAbstractTableModel for each table to manage the data. The model's data() should supply the appropriate text for name and preview columns, and handle the checkbox and button in the first column (via delegates or item flags). The 'preview' for sequence or match can be a truncated version of the full string/hex/regex for quick viewing. Ensure the full values are still accessible via tooltip or on click. The data model should also track the enabled/disabled state of responses (for the checkbox column). This model will be populated when importing the JSON or when adding entries programmatically.

steps.name: Implement Response Matching and Actions
steps.details: Tie the Responses list to incoming log data so that when an enabled response's pattern matches new incoming text from the COM port, the specified response action occurs. This means in the COM port reading logic (where new lines are read and appended), check each enabled Response entry: if the line matches the entry's match (using the appropriate string, hex, or regex comparison), then execute the defined response. Executing a response can include: sending an action (if `action_id` is specified, find that Action and send it; if an inline `action` is specified, send that sequence):contentReference[oaicite:8]{index=8}, inserting a comment line into the log (use the provided comment text, and if `timestamp` is true, prepend or format with timestamp), inserting an extra line break if `linebreak` is true, taking a snapshot if `snapshot` is true (if KLogg supports snapshot functionality), and closing the COM port if `stop_communication` is true (gracefully disconnect). Implement these so that multiple responses can trigger if their patterns match, but ensure that actions like stop_communication break out of any further processing as needed. The goal is to automate reactions to specific incoming log patterns using the configuration from the Responses table.
